summary: Availability: isDebug=true Returns the Raw SOAP Request With the Sabre Account Username in Clear Text (also: TC-NEXTAVAIL-SEC-03)
spec_ref: SPEC.md §7.14 (debug payload must not expose credentials); CSV TC-AVAIL-SEC-05 / TC-NEXTAVAIL-SEC-03
expected_value: HTTP 200. If supplierRequest/supplierResponse are returned at all, they contain no username, password, PCC/session token or API key (SPEC §7.14): the WS-Security header is removed or fully masked.
impact: Any API consumer can read a live supplier account identifier and the full supplier message flow, which helps account abuse and supplier-side enumeration.
evidence: With `"isDebug": true`, Availability and NextAvailability add `supplierRequest` and `supplierResponse` (the full Sabre SOAP request and a ~60 KB response) to the body. The request contains the WS-Security header with `<wsse:UsernameToken><wsse:Username>` holding the Sabre account username in clear text (the password element is masked as `***`). summary: Availability: Passenger Count Sent as a String Is Accepted (also: no other test case)
spec_ref: CSV TC-AVAIL-NEG-10 (a string count must be rejected)
expected_value: HTTP 400 standard error envelope (Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context) naming passengers[0].count as the wrong type.
impact: Clients can send malformed bodies that work today and break when the parser is tightened.
evidence: A request whose `passengers[0].count` is the JSON string "2" is accepted and answered with HTTP 200 and journeys, instead of being rejected as a wrong type. Same behaviour as the Galileo/EGY run on ne-4 (its BUG-09).

summary: NextAvailability: NextAvailability Accepts the availabilityId of One Search With the responseId of Another (also: no other test case)
spec_ref: CSV TC-NEXTAVAIL-NEG-10 (cross-identifier pair must be rejected); SPEC §3 id chaining
expected_value: HTTP 400 or 404 standard error envelope stating that availabilityId and responseId do not belong together.
impact: Pages can be returned for the wrong search/session, which breaks the integrity of the paging chain and weakens session isolation.
evidence: NextAvailability called with the `availabilityId` of search A (CAI-JED +30) and the `responseId` of search B (CAI-JED +31) returns HTTP 200 and a page 2 instead of being rejected. The pair is not validated for consistency, so the page that comes back cannot be attributed to either search. SelectAvailability rejects the same kind of mixed pair on the other suppliers; Galileo/EGY on ne-4 has the same defect on NextAvailability (its BUG-05).

summary: SelectAvailability: bookingClassIds in the Documented Nested Shape Is Rejected (Only a Flat List Works) (also: no other test case)
spec_ref: Postman collection "NDC Integrations_Ancillary Galileo avilability" (SelectAvailability body); CSV TC-SELECTAVAIL-POS-01
expected_value: The collection body is accepted (HTTP 200 with responseId and offerId), or the contract difference is documented and the 400 names `bookingClassIds` and the expected shape.
impact: The Availability flow cannot be driven from the shared collection for SabreNdc without per-supplier request shapes.
evidence: The Postman collection (and the Galileo/EGY implementation on ne-4) sends `bookingClassIds` as `{ "<journeyRefId>": { "<segmentRefId>": ["<bookingClassId>"] } }`. summary: FareConfirm: FareConfirm Offer Carries RBD N After Booking Code Y Was Selected on SelectAvailability (also: no other test case)
spec_ref: CSV TC-FARECONFIRM-INT-03 (RBD of the offer equals the selected bookingCode); SPEC §2.2 FareConfirm
expected_value: rbd of each offer segment equals the selected booking code (Y); a different class is only acceptable if the response says the requested class was replaced.
impact: The caller may book and be charged for a different fare class than the one chosen, with fare rules (change/refund/baggage) of that other class.
evidence: After SelectAvailability with booking code Y on every segment of a connecting CAI-JED journey (QR1310 + QR1190), FareConfirm returns the same two flights in the same order but the `rbd` of the offer segments is `N`, not the selected `Y`. The CSV defines a different RBD as "wrong inventory priced". It is not known from the response whether the price is the Y or the N fare; the offer should state the class that was actually priced and that was selected.

summary: FareConfirm: FareConfirm Does Not Validate ResponseId (Wrong, Mismatched or Missing Value Accepted) (also: TC-FARECONFIRM-NEG-03, TC-FARECONFIRM-NEG-04)
expected_value: HTTP 4xx standard error envelope (Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context) for a wrong, mismatched or missing ResponseId.
impact: The request contract is not enforced: a client that sends wrong or no session id still gets a price, which hides integration errors and weakens session binding.
evidence: FareConfirm answers HTTP 200 with a priced offer when `ResponseId` is the id of the Availability response instead of the Select response, when it comes from selection A while `selectedOfferId` comes from selection B, and when `ResponseId` is omitted altogether. Only `selectedOfferId` is evaluated. Same behaviour as Galileo/EGY on ne-4 (its BUG-06).
